title: Run-quality benchmarking of a dispatched agent's own transcript — trajectory evaluation, deduction scoring, and the subject-class gate
summary: Prep research for a hash-keyed decision under #3383 (report we:reports/2026-09-12-run-quality-benchmark-for-dispatched-agent-runs.md): should a dispatched background agent's own transcript be reviewed for HOW it ran, scored as a benchmark where every run starts at an implicit 100% and each criterion is a deduction, with low-risk findings auto-applied and larger ones filed? THE GAP IS REAL AND IT IS THE RUN PATH -- five adjacent mechanisms exist and none is this: we:skills-src/inspect-agent-health/agent-health.mjs classifies liveness only (ACTIVE/BLOCKED_ON_CHILD/BLOCKED_ON_TOOL/IDLE_OR_STALLED); we:scripts/conveyor/hiccup-classify.mjs classifies blocking delivery hiccups off tick state; we:scripts/operations/review-pr.mjs reviews the DIFF (its op declaration takes exactly pr + repo, its judge shape asks for 'one sentence on the diff as a whole') and we:scripts/operations/review-dispatch.mjs's entire brief vocabulary is PR/REPO/SESSION_SLUG, so no operation in the repo takes an agent's own run as its subject; the learnings pool collects self-reported observations; the driver watchdog watches the driver process. THE FIELD ALREADY NAMES THE MECHANISM -- 'trajectory evaluation', which independently names the operator's criteria (Redundant Tool Calls, Tool Frequency, Task Relevance, Execution Efficiency) and argues in the same terms that an agent reaching the right answer via a wildly inefficient path is still a production failure. THE ANALOGY BREAKS IN ONE LOAD-BEARING PLACE -- published trajectory evals get comparability from a FIXED TASK SET; here every run is a different item, size, model and effort tier, so this is not a benchmark in the SWE-bench/MCP-Bench sense and must not inherit their comparability. THREE MATURE FIELD-DATA SCORING SYSTEMS EACH SETTLE ONE SUB-QUESTION -- Lighthouse (per-metric scores are the record, the 0-100 headline is derived, weights are versioned, history is NEVER re-normalised, cross-version comparison is meaningless); aviation FOQA exceedance detection (thresholds sit in a zone APPROACHING a limit so routine flights register exceedances as a matter of course, and a singular exceedance may not trigger corrective action at all -- mitigation follows the AGGREGATE rate); chess engine accuracy (90-100% is grandmaster level and grandmasters routinely score below 100). THE RISK DIAL AND ITS GATE ARE ALREADY RATIFIED HERE -- assessMissingOperationConfidence (we:scripts/conveyor/hiccup-classify.mjs) returns {selfClears, batched, escalate} from a blacklist check plus five confidence criteria, which IS the low-risk-auto-applies split; fileHiccup (we:scripts/conveyor/hiccup-sink.mjs) writes an approvalPending entry into the same pool, we:scripts/conveyor/hiccup-approve.mjs clears it, and one line of we:scripts/conveyor/learnings-harvest.mjs holds a gated entry out of clustering. What does NOT transfer is #3422's own AXIS ('did the tick get blocked'), under which a finding on a SUCCESSFUL run is non-blocking and therefore routes to 'file the card only, no fix proposed' -- the opposite of auto-applying. THE POOL CANNOT HOLD A SCORECARD -- learnings-drop's ALLOWED_KEYS is an allow-list that REJECTS unknown keys and FIELD_CAPS caps summary at 240 chars, so the score needs its own store; the precedent is we:scripts/check-app-conformance.mjs, which computes a rounded percentage that DEFAULTS TO 100 when nothing was measured and appends one row per run to a burndown JSON. THE SUBJECT MIGHT ITSELF BE A LIVE DRIVER -- a conveyor runner holds a queue and dispatches other work while its own transcript is read; auto-applying a fix around it on an external judge's say-so bypasses every refusal the watchdog/validate-and-promote design encodes (last-known-good recorded not inferred; long quiet period AND no in-flight work AND a live lease before acting). The repo already ruled the neighbouring case: #2077's rider, codified under #pr-flow-rollout-mechanism, holds that a run's own executing tooling is never modified in the checkout a live run executes it from, citing uniform CI prior art (GitHub Actions pins the workflow definition at run start, Jenkins pins shared-library versions per run, merge bots run from a deployment outside the tree they land). The two rules key on different tests -- #2077 on the edit's TOUCH-SET, this one on the SUBJECT CLASS -- so they compose rather than duplicate. SHARED CODE IS SHARED FAILURE -- the driver watchdog's header states the rule and its suite asserts the import graph with exact equality so the allow-list cannot be widened silently; a run-quality scorer inherits the same reflexivity since a dispatched run's quality is partly a property of the dispatcher. THE SCOPE IS SMALLER THAN THE FRAMING ASSUMED -- #3475 (resolved, codified at #automated-session-introspection) already ratifies a detached judge pass over a real transcript at three triggers, of which the reaper and SessionEnd reach a dispatched lane agent (a top-level session, not an Agent-tool subagent, so SubagentStop does not); that is the READER, and what a criteria-expansion of it cannot give you is a score, a rubric version, a trend, a subject-class gate or an auto-apply path. One concrete gap: no dispatch record stores a transcript path, and the existing resolver probes only the nested subagents directory, so it would miss a dispatched lane agent today.
